**Visual Analysis of Test Image:**
- Corn plants at vegetative stage
- Leaves show broad, pale yellow-green streaks/bands running parallel to the midrib along the full leaf length
- Multiple plants affected
- No discrete spots or lesions — diffuse, longitudinal striping pattern
- Plants appear somewhat stunted

**Reasoning:**
The broad, pale yellow-green longitudinal streaking affecting multiple leaves is the key feature. Maize streak virus (MSV) typically produces narrow, fine, discontinuous white/yellow streaks — the reference collage confirms this thin-streak pattern. The test image has much broader, more diffuse pale banding across the leaf surface, which is more consistent with **Stewarts wilt**, where the bacterial pathogen causes long, irregular pale-green to yellow streaks with wavy margins running parallel to leaf veins, often affecting young plants early in the season.
